problems: Where the specs disagree I followed topic ownership (specs/README.md §3.3) and the assignment. ps and top use the kernel spec §3.18 layout (default `PID TTY STAT TIME COMMAND`, 3-letter STAT codes); free, vmstat, pmap and swapctl use memory spec §3.17; predict uses predictive-prefetch.md §3.8 (`-n`, `--why`; the shell spec's `-k` and `--explain` kept as aliases; exit codes 0/1/2); ai uses agentic-shell.md §3.3 (exit codes 0-4, `-n/--dry-run`, `log --all`). The man pages were updated to match.

Two shell-spec SYS-02 session checks will not match this output. Step 20 expects `budget` in `free` output, but memory spec §3.17.1 labels that column `total`. Step 17 uses `ps -o cmd`; that works because `cmd` is accepted as an alias.

Protocol `ProcInfo` lacks sid, tty, fg, leader, boosted, exclusive, overSoftLimit, pinned, overruns, kind and exit. ps and top read them when present and otherwise show `?` or `-`. Default ps selection falls back to the caller's uid and session.

Protocol `MemStat` and `ProcDetail.pages` lack pinned, avail, local swap cap, device, upload queue, pagesIn/pagesOut, bytesUploaded, per-process swap split, working set, last page-in time, and per-page kind, label, copies, sha256, gen and pin reasons. Those columns print `-` (lib/mem.ts). vmstat's us/ke/id and top's Sched line and CPU split need a `sched.info` call.

Protocol `bootlog` returns only log lines, the critical-path names and a total, with `boot: current|previous`. bootlog derives timings from each service's first and last log line. `--list` reports ENOSYS, and `--boot N` accepts only current/previous (or 0, -1, 1).
Protocol `fsck` has no `path` and no directory or user counts. PATH appears only in the `--checksum` line; `--server` sends `scope: 'both'`.
Protocol `Stat` has no sync state, so stat prints `Sync: -` unless the kernel adds a `sync` field. `Quota` has no confirmation time, so quota prints `source: server` without `(confirmed HH:MM:SS)`.
Protocol `find` returns only a count of denied directories, so find and du print `'<start>': Permission denied (N directories skipped)` instead of one line per directory.
The `id` syscall with `{user}` does not exist in protocol; id, chown, find -user, ps -u and quota -u use `users.list`. `reboot` has no verbose flag, so `--verbose` warns and restarts without it.

Interactive top cannot read keys without blocking (no timed read or poll call). It redraws every delay and exits cleanly on SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP (caught through sig.action); the k, r, P, M, T and s keys are not implemented yet.

The `ai` front end cannot import ai/ (boundary rule). It starts the agent from the manifest `/bin/lib/ai.agent.json` with argv `['ai', ...flags, instruction]` and passes its exit status through. That manifest path is my assumption and needs confirming by R4.
find.ts imports `matchGlob` from the shell agent's apps/shell/glob.ts to avoid a second glob implementation. A signature change there would break find.
No DSA structure is implemented. svcctl leaves cycle detection to the kernel's requested `svc.verify` (ENOSYS today); without it `require` keeps the edit and says the graph could not be verified.
